rationale: Both candidates miss the ground truth's most severe finding (fork-PR sandbox/security execution risk) and most of its specific line-level nits (diffusion link, untracked-file staleness, git-diff-excludes-untracked, HEAD==head_sha insufficiency). X partially echoes the 'merge gate stricter than policy' and fingerprint-adequacy themes across its P1/P2 findings and is broader (7 well-evidenced findings with concrete fixes and code snippets), while Y is tighter with 3 findings, one of which (skill-name $-prefix inconsistency) is a fairly direct hit on a ground-truth item, though its conclusion is weaker than the ground truth's diagnosis. Precision and grounding are comparably strong for both; X edges ahead on actionability and overall depth.
